title: Reproductive Synchrony of a Tropical Shrub: Experimental Studies on Effects of Pollinators and Seed Predators in Hybanthus Prunifolius (Violaceae)
screening_reason: Direct plant reproductive success and experimental pollinator/seed-predator effects are compared for plants flowering in versus out of synchrony with the plant population, but the timing exposure is conspecific flowering synchrony rather than temporal matching to an independently measured animal activity window.
notes: Augspurger 1981; high-value prior art on population reproductive synchrony, outside strict plant-partner H1.

title: Insect Seed Predators in Erythrina falcata (Fabaceae): Identification of Predatory Species and Ecological Consequences of Asynchronous Flowering
screening_reason: Trees were classified early/peak/late and seed predation was 65%/80%/50%, directly supporting temporal escape, but the endpoint is predation rate rather than a final plant reproductive/fitness measure and no independent predator activity curve yields strict synchrony.
notes: Pereira et al. 2014; tropical escape-in-time system. Five generalist seed-predator species identified.

title: Genetic variation in flowering phenology and avoidance of seed predation in native populations of Ulex europaeus
screening_reason: Common-garden flowering types show genetic differences and reduce seed predation via temporal escape or predator satiation, but strict plant-predator activity overlap plus final fitness is not jointly identified on the IWE scale.
notes: Atlan et al. 2010; valuable evolutionary timing-defense context.

title: Timing of Flowering: Opposed Selection on Different Fitness Components and Trait Covariation
screening_reason: Seven-year Lathyrus vernus study connects flowering start to seed set, predispersal seed predation, grazing and lifetime-fitness proxies, but does not estimate one plant-partner synchrony exposure for the interacting animals.

title: Plant-animal interactions mediate climatic effects on selection on flowering time
screening_reason: Twenty-one-year Lathyrus vernus study measures plant fitness plus grazing and predispersal seed predation and explicitly studies climate-mediated relative timing, but interaction intensity/covariance rather than a direct animal-activity overlap metric drives the analysis.
notes: Valdés & Ehrlén 2021; long-term mediation evidence. Same broader Lathyrus programme as IWE052; dependence required.
